name: Question 9
problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.5$ | $0$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.5$ | $0$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.5$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.7$ | $0.3$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =1\cdot 0.5+3\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5+1.5 \\  & =2 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =2\cdot 0.7+4\cdot 0.3 \\  & =1.4+1.2 \\  & =2.6\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-2)(y-2.6)f(x,y) \\  & =(1-2)(2-2.6)f(1,2) \\  & +(1-2)(4-2.6)f(1,4) \\  & +(3-2)(2-2.6)f(3,2) \\  & +(3-2)(4-2.6)f(3,4) \\  & =(-1)(-0.6)(0.5) \\  & +(-1)(1.4)(0) \\  & +(1)(-0.6)(0.2) \\  & +(1)(1.4)(0.3) \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The covariance of two discrete random variables X and Y with joint support S is defined as

Cov[X,Y]=∑(x,y)∈S(x−E[X])(y−E[Y])f(x,y).

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for X and Y. These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

f Y=2 Y=4 fX
X=1 0.5 0 0.5
X=3 0.2 0.3 0.5
fY 0.7 0.3 1

We now compute E[X] and E[Y], as follows:

E[X]=∑x∈SXx⋅fX(x)=1⋅0.5+3⋅0.5=0.5+1.5=2E[Y]=∑y∈SYy⋅fY(y)=2⋅0.7+4⋅0.3=1.4+1.2=2.6

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

Cov[X,Y]=∑(x,y)∈S(x−E[X])(y−E[Y])f(x,y)=∑(x,y)∈S(x−2)(y−2.6)f(x,y)=(1−2)(2−2.6)f(1,2)=+(1−2)(4−2.6)f(1,4)=+(3−2)(2−2.6)f(3,2)=+(3−2)(4−2.6)f(3,4)=(−1)(−0.6)(0.5)=+(−1)(1.4)(0)=+(1)(−0.6)(0.2)=+(1)(1.4)(0.3)=0.6.
